title: Session of Harvestwood PCA vs. New River Presbytery (Complaint)
disposition_detail: Issue decided: Yes—Presbytery erred in making final disposition of a matter that came only as a BCO 41-3 reference seeking advice (lines 50–56). Complaint sustained on that procedural/jurisdictional ground. The SJC remanded/recommended that NRP rescind its March 15, 1997 action and clarify the teacher's views through proper BCO procedures, either by advice upon a clearer record or by a reference for final disposition (line 95). It expressly declined to rule on the creation/theistic-evolution merits (line 91).
first_summary: Harvestwood complained after New River Presbytery declared a Sunday school teacher eligible to teach despite his exception on origins. The SJC found NRP had received Grace Covenant's inquiry as a BCO 41 reference seeking advice, yet issued a final eligibility decision without original jurisdiction or an adequate record of the teacher's beliefs. It sustained the complaint, recommended that NRP rescind its March 15, 1997 action and clarify the teacher's views, and declined to decide the creation/theistic-evolution issue.
summary: New River Presbytery treated Grace Covenant PCA's BCO 41 inquiry about a Sunday school teacher's acceptability as a request for advice, but then ruled he was eligible to teach. On Harvestwood's complaint, the SJC held NRP erred: it lacked original jurisdiction absent review, appeal, complaint, or reference for final disposition, and the record was unclear about the teacher's views. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded, directing NRP to rescind its March 15, 1997 action and clarify his views through proper BCO procedures; it declined to reach the creation/theistic-evolution merits.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 97-13 and title appear at lines 3, 14, and 16; SJC/26th Assembly (1998) at line 3. The preliminary judgment was authored by TE Paul B. Fowler with TE Paul D. Kooistra and RE John Van Voorhis (lines 97–99) and adopted by SJC vote: 17 concurring, 1 recused, 6 absent (line 103). Source path/hash as above.
evidence_notes.dispute: HCPCA complained after NRP's March 15, 1997 response declared the teacher eligible to teach, and after NRP denied that complaint on July 12, 1997; the complaint was appealed to the SJC on July 30, 1997 (lines 44–46). The framed issue was whether Presbytery erred in making final disposition of a matter that came to it only as a reference seeking advice (lines 50–52).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Judgment: Yes (line 56). NRP properly understood GCPCA's communication as a BCO 41-3 reference seeking advice, but instead issued a final eligibility decision without original jurisdiction and without a clear record (lines 60–62). The SJC said the local Session has responsibility under BCO 12-5; Presbytery may assume original jurisdiction only by review, appeal, complaint, or reference for final disposition (line 62). The record was inadequate concerning the teacher's beliefs (lines 64–75, 87–89). The SJC declined to pronounce on biblical creation (line 91) and recommended NRP rescind its March 15, 1997 action and clarify the person's views through appropriate BCO means (line 95).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The complainants' arguments about theistic evolution and the 1990 ruling, and NRP's contrary reading of that ruling, were not resolved on the merits (lines 79–85). The SJC expressly declined to reach the creation issue because the record was inadequate (line 91). Historical matters—the 1988–1990 dispute and 1996 General Assembly exception—are background, not the challenged action (lines 20–48). The source gives the SJC preliminary judgment, not later Assembly action or implementation.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Prior SJC case 90-3 and General Assembly actions are referenced as history/background (lines 24, 40, 48), but no incorporated decision is supplied for their terms. The decision here is the 1997-13 preliminary judgment and SJC vote (lines 97–103); no separate opinions are reported beyond the concurrence/author note and voting tally.

source_limits: The source contains the SJC preliminary judgment, reasoning, and voting tally only. The record of the case (ROC) is excerpted, not reproduced, so the factual dispute about what the teacher believed cannot be independently assessed. No later General Assembly action, final implementation, or full record is supplied. The header's 'recommended for remand' is treated as metadata consistent with the body's recommendation to rescind and clarify through proper BCO procedures.
